title: Static analysis (SAST): configuring, tuning and living with false positives

videos.script: A scanner that finds four hundred problems on its first run is a scanner nobody reads again. {{venv}} That is how most teams meet static analysis. Today you meet it properly, on linkbox. {{bandit}} Static analysis reads code without running it. It matches the code against rules somebody wrote. Anything that only exists while the program runs is out of its sight. {{rules}} You start with Bandit, and its first run reads the wrong files. You narrow what it reads. Then you quiet one rule in the tests, without switching it off anywhere else. {{tuned}} Next you write two rules of your own, with Semgrep. One of them knows something no general tool could know. It knows how linkbox decides who may write. {{semgrep}} The pipeline gets a new stage, and the first push breaks the build. That is the point. You fix both findings. Each fix comes with a test that fails first and passes after. {{green}} One finding stays open on purpose, with a reason written down. Lesson 6 closes it.
